An advertisement targeting the tobacco industry can indeed affect young people's perception of smoking in movies and their intention to smoke. According to a real-world study, placing an antismoking advertisement before movies containing smoking scenes can help to immunize non-smokers against the influences of film stars' smoking. However, it's crucial to exercise caution in the type of advertisement screened, as some types of advertising may reinforce smokers' intentions to smoke. 

Additionally, it's worth noting that restricting access to movies that depict smoking, such as R-rated movies, can also reduce adolescent smoking susceptibility. Parental restriction of R-rated movie viewing has been associated with both lower adolescent smoking susceptibility and lower smoking rates. 

Overall, a well-designed advertisement targeting the tobacco industry, combined with other strategies such as parental restriction of movie viewing, can be an effective way to reduce young people's intention to smoke and ultimately decrease smoking rates.
